analysis_role: Post-result mechanism-discrimination boundary test using only frozen BIO15, BIO1, coarse geography, the nine-taxon orientation panel and six accepted topologies.

incremental_prediction.baseline: BIO1 + latitude + longitude + Brownian conditional prediction
incremental_prediction.interpretation: Orientation does not improve held-out BIO15 prediction beyond BIO1, coarse geography and Brownian covariance in this n=9 panel.

interpretation.bio15: The BIO15 coefficient retains its positive sign on every accepted topology after conditioning on BIO1 and coarse geography, but sign stability falls to 48/54 species-LOO fits, the adjusted coefficient is not threshold-supported, orientation worsens held-out BIO15 prediction on every topology, and nearest opposite-state taxon pairs are directionally mixed. BIO15 therefore persists as a component of the present climatic contrast but is not isolated as a specific explanatory axis.
interpretation.bio1: BIO1 retains the prespecified negative orientation direction in 54/54 species-LOO fits after conditioning on BIO15 and geography, but the adjusted coefficient is also not threshold-supported and matched-pair contrasts are mixed. The current data therefore support a composite climatic/lineage correspondence rather than a unique BIO15 or BIO1 cause.

claim_ceiling: No result establishes precipitation seasonality or temperature as a selective agent or historical cause.
No result establishes a hydric or thermal mechanism, adaptation or plasticity.
Matched extant taxon pairs are not reconstructed independent transitions.
BIO15 and BIO1 may reflect correlated present climatic regimes and unmeasured lineage/geographic properties.
No additional environmental predictor may be added after result inspection.
